summary: The revised contracts now cover the RuntimeTool and SecurityTool dimension ceilings with concrete, independent runtime and negative-security oracles. Current targeted executions are non-empty and pass, including the release durable-performance envelope and attacker-CA rejection. The remaining defect is structural false-green protection: Cargo and meter return success for zero matching tests, but the EC runners do not independently require a non-zero executed-test count, so the declared zero-suite fail-closed behavior is not enforced.
findings: Performance EC cases `relay-competitor-performance-behavior` and `relay-competitor-performance-measured-durable-lifecycle` / claim `normalized-win-ratchet-decision-model` do not fail closed when their Cargo filters execute zero tests. The exact-filter efficiency command can return exit 0 after a rename or removed `#[test]`, in which case `measured_durable_lifecycle_gate` never performs its one-report/non-zero-sample assertions; `meter test` only forwards the child exit code and does not reject a zero-test summary. Revise `apps/relay/external-contracts/competitor-performance/efficiency/perf-gate.md` and its vat runner so an outer oracle requires the expected named tests and a non-zero execution count (for the efficiency gate, exactly one passed gate plus the `relay_perf_gate` report marker) before accepting the measurement.

Security EC cases `relay-security-hardening-auth-and-admission-behavior`, `relay-security-hardening-negative-peer-and-kubernetes-boundaries`, `relay-security-hardening-guard-scan`, and `relay-security-hardening-rotation-and-peer-stability` do not enforce their claimed zero-suite failure. Their Cargo/meter commands pass when existing test binaries contain zero matching tests, and Guard treats the meter evidence as clean from exit status alone. Revise `apps/relay/external-contracts/security-hardening/security/security-evidence.md` and `guard-security` runner to assert the required named auth, admission, attacker-CA, trusted-peer, Kubernetes, and reload tests are present and that each required suite executes a non-zero count before Guard can report clean.
